nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What are some of the negative consequences of asymmetric power in supplier-retailer relationships according to Johnsen et al. (2020)?
nodes.answer: Johnsen et al. (2020) suggest that asymmetric power in supplier-retailer relationships can lead to a hegemony that results in excessive influence, sustains economic privilege, pushes suppliers towards abusive labour practices, and encourages a focus on short-term goals.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Supporting diverse suppliers_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does power imbalance in supplier-retailer relationships impact the weaker party's behaviour, as mentioned by Aboulic & Walker (2015)?
nodes.answer: According to Aboulic & Walker (2015), power asymmetry in such relationships affects the adaptive and collaborative behaviour of the weaker party, potentially leading the powerful party to act opportunistically within the relationship.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Responsible purchasing habits|Supporting diverse suppliers_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does uniform asymmetry manifest in fashion supplier-retailer relationships?
nodes.answer: Uniform asymmetry is evident as the retailer dominates and controls supply chain relationships to achieve its sustainability goals unilaterally, providing very little room for suppliers to raise their voices in Supplier Performance Development (SPD) within relationships.
